headline: A Korean report says SK Hynix is struggling to develop a chip-stacking method called hybrid bonding while Samsung is reportedly already sending samples to customers.
score_reason: Lowered from 5: the claim dates from 7 Oct, rests on unnamed technical staff quoted by one Korean outlet and is confirmed by neither company.
importance_line: It bears on the race between Samsung and SK Hynix to supply the fast memory used in AI chips, which matters to AI chip makers and their buyers, but neither company has confirmed it and sending samples is not mass production.
summary: BigGo Finance reports, citing the Korean outlet Damnang on 7 Oct 2026, that SK Hynix has run into difficulties developing hybrid bonding (joining stacked memory chips directly with copper instead of tiny solder bumps) for next-generation high-bandwidth memory, while Samsung Electronics is said to be already supplying customers with samples built with it. Neither company has confirmed this and the report names no memory generation or customer; separately, Counterpoint Research data show Samsung's share of high-bandwidth memory rising from 21% to 33% between the first and second quarters, against 30% for SK Hynix, although BigGo cautions that SK Hynix's figures use different measures.
notes: Underlying Damnang report is from 7 Oct. A similar headline (SK hynix reportedly faces difficulties in HBM hybrid bonding) was in the 8 Oct pool but is not in any 6 to 9 Oct edition. BigGo itself says it is premature to judge the gap between the firms.
